title: Adaptive proportional trip controller with simulated canary and safe reroute playbook
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Goal: Implement an adaptive proportional trip controller (APTC) that computes dynamic trip thresholds per dependency/model/tenant using workload-aware statistics and simulation-driven calibrations. The controller should: 1) maintain SLOs (p95 latency & p99 tail; error-rate budgets) by gracefully shedding traffic based on proportional weights rather than hard binary trips, 2) support multi-region prioritized failover with capacity-aware routing and capacity-aware shedding, 3) provide a deterministic safe fallback chain (model variant -> lower-quality replica -> cached response -> synthetic fallback) and 4) enable simulated canary runs and shadow testing before enabling aggressive shedding in production.
background: We currently have coarse fuse behaviour in the runtime: many dependencies use fixed threshold breakers (latency or error-rate) that hard trip and reroute to fallback models. This causes sudden user-visible regressions during bursty spikes and cross-region incidents. Several prior tickets explore tenant-aware tripping and staged fallbacks but lack a unified, simulation-first calibration approach. The APTC is intended to reduce flapping and provide stable degradation curves while preserving highest-priority tenants during multi-region failover.
acceptance_criteria: APTC computes per-entity trip score combining latency percentiles, short-window error rate, and token-cost pressure
Proportional shedding reduces incoming RPS according to a continuous weight in [0.0,1.0] rather than an immediate hard circuit open
Fallback chain selection follows deterministic rules and attaches metadata for observability (reason, triggered_by, chosen_fallback, capacity_estimate)
Simulation harness empircally suggests default calibration for common workloads (chat, completion, embeddings) and provides a 'safety margin' parameter
Canary pipeline supports shadow replay of 5-10% traffic, and a dry-run mode that reports suggested shedding decisions without applying them
End-to-end latency and error SLO regressions measured in a staged environment are < 5% relative to existing baseline for normal load, and degradation is smooth under synthetic overload
Operational runbook documented and added to Console runbooks with alert thresholds and rollback instructions
design_decisions: Score composition: use rolling-window percentiles (p50, p90, p95) + exponential weighted error rate + token pressure score; combine with tunable coefficients to produce a single trip_score [0-1]
Proportional shedding: map trip_score to shed_fraction via monotonic transfer function (sigmoid with configurable midpoint) to avoid oscillations

Hysteresis: require sustained trip_score above threshold for 'warmup_duration' before increasing shed_fraction; when score decreases, reduce shed_fraction with slower decay to avoid immediate reopen flapping

Multi-region priority: attach region_priority and route to regions in order while checking remote capacity_estimates; if downstream region indicates low capacity, increase local shedding rather than redirecting
Fallback chain: prefer model-variant downgrade (e.g., quantized variant), then cached prefix response, then a lightweight template fallback; fallbacks must be tagged and traced for quality monitoring
Simulation-first: run a binary-search calibration in the sim harness to recommend default sigmoid midpoint and steepness values for each workload class
Observability: emit per-request 'decision envelope' with debug flags only in trace samples; aggregate circuit metrics per-tenant, per-model, per-region in Console
implementation_notes: Components: 1) controller service (stateless HTTP endpoint) computes trip_score from realtime metrics and returns shed_fraction + fallback_hint, 2) local runtime shaper applies shed_fraction probabilistically per-request (deterministic hashing for idempotency), 3) routing layer consults fallback_hint to pick next path, 4) sim harness (offline) runs replayed traces and synthetic overload patterns to calibrate controller parameters. Use percentile streaming (TDigest-like) and EWMA counters. Keep controller decisions idempotent for retries. Ensure controller is highly available; fall back to default conservative shedding if controller unreachable.
work_breakdown: APTC core library: trip_score calculation, hysteresis and transfer functions (eng-2 weeks)
Controller service API and HA deployment (eng-1 week)
Local runtime integration: probabilistic shaper and deterministic hashing (eng-2 weeks)
Routing fallback integration and multi-region capacity signals (eng-2 weeks)
Simulation harness and calibration jobs with dashboards (eng-2 weeks)
End-to-end tests and staged canary (eng + se-1 week)
Runbook, alerts, and Console metrics + trace plumbing (ops + product-1 week)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive shedding could reduce revenue for high-value tenants. Mitigation: support per-tenant overrides and prioritize by tenant SLA weight; default conservative coefficients and require canary promotion
Risk: Controller becomes single point of failure. Mitigation: controller returns conservative shedding when unresponsive; local runtime has fallback policies and cached heuristics

Risk: False positives due to noisy percentile estimates for low-volume tenants. Mitigation: require minimum traffic thresholds for per-tenant scoring, fall back to cohort-level signals when below threshold

Risk: Complexity of multi-region coordination could increase latency. Mitigation: use asynchronous capacity signals and avoid synchronous cross-region calls in the hot path; decisions favor local safety
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha Banerjee: Initial spike of notes from architecture review. Agreed to prefer proportional shedding vs multi-tiered hard trips. Action: prototype transfer functions (sigmoid and linear) and run sim with existing traces.

2026-03-01 - Miguel Santos: Prototype completed; ran replay of last 7 days of chat traffic. Sigmoid midpoint 0.6 produced smooth degradation; p95 target maintained in most scenarios. Observed edge case where sudden token-price spikes led to rapid ramp-up; added token-pressure coefficient.

2026-03-08 - QA (Priya Nair): created test plan for staged canary with shadow traffic at 5% and 10%. Will verify that shadow decisions match applied decisions in dry-run mode.

2026-03-10 - Miguel Santos: Integration PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2143. Includes controller API, shaper hook, and sim harness. Request review from @infra-team and @observability.

notes: Do not enable aggressive shedding by default. Feature-flag gating required; rollout via staged canary with explicit operator approval. Ensure billing and SLA teams are notified before high-shed trials.
